Subject: Model catalog provenance + version pinning questionnaire

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the product overview yesterday. Our security team has a short questionnaire focused on your model catalog and licensing/provenance controls — specifically how you attest origins, support version pinning for deployed endpoints, and communicate model updates to customers.

I've attached their worksheet (attached: GB_RFI_model_catalog.xlsx). Can you fill this out and return by EOD next Tuesday? A few items we need called out:
- Worldwide redistribution / attribution obligations for open-source-derived checkpoints
- How you record model origin and software SBOMs for models in the catalog
- Recommended process for customers who want to pin a model and request signed attestations for a specific binary/version
- Our auditor will expect accessible evidence links (drive or signed artifact) and a contact for followups

Please CC procurement (procurement@globalbank.com) when you reply.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@globalbank.com>
Cc: procurement@globalbank.com
Date: 2026-11-16T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model catalog provenance + version pinning questionnaire

Lisa — thanks for the clear ask.

Quick plan:
- I've started the answers in the attached workbook (GlobalBank_RFI_model_catalog_answers_v1.xlsx).
- For legal/licensing language and SBOM export we want a quick pass from Monica (legal/compliance) to ensure we provide attestations in an auditor-friendly format.
- Can you confirm whether your auditor needs signed binary checksums or if a signed manifest + Drive link suffices?

High-level on the bullets you listed (summary, see workbook for details):
- Redistribution & attribution: we include license metadata for each catalog item and surface license obligations in the model details page and API. For redistribution customers are responsible for complying with upstream licenses; Redwood provides the license text and a recommended attribution template.
- Model origin / SBOM: models in our catalog include provenance metadata (origin repo/link, model hash, training dataset provenance tags, and a basic SBOM for runtime dependencies). For curated/verified models we include a provenance certificate (PDF) that contains the digest, source URL, and curator assertion.
- Version pinning & attestations: customers can pin model versions on the Redwood Console or via API. For pinned versions we can export a signed manifest (PKCS7) containing the model digest, build date, and serving binary version. We can also generate a PDF attestation on request (requires an enterprise support ticket for signing).
- Evidence links: we can provide time-stamped Drive links and signed manifests. If you need HSM-signed attestations we can scope that in the contract.

Sharing with internal reviewers: forwarding to Monica and Neha for legal/compliance/localization on wording.

Thanks — expect a reviewed workbook back by Mon/Tue next week.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
(attachment: GlobalBank_RFI_model_catalog_answers_v1.xlsx)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-18T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Model catalog provenance + version pinning questionnaire — legal review

Sean — quick review below and suggested wording edits for the workbook and the provenance certificate. High-level comments:

1) Licensing & redistribution
- Keep the customer-facing language: "Customers are responsible for compliance with third-party model licenses." Add a second sentence for auditors: "Redwood maintains accompanying license metadata and historical snapshots for all catalog items as provided by the model curator or upstream source."

2) SBOM & runtime dependencies
- Recommend we include a minimal SBOM (package names + versions) for the serving stack only; for training data provenance we should include tags/notes but avoid providing raw datasets.

3) Signed attestations & pinning
- To avoid regulatory exposure, propositional signed attestations should be offered as an add-on deliverable. Suggested language: "Redwood can provide signed manifests containing model digest, build metadata, and signing authority identity. Production-grade HSM signing is offered via Redwood Private or as a contract add-on."

4) Evidence retention and access
- Add retention clause: "Signed manifests and provenance certificates are retained for a minimum of 2 years by default; longer retention available under contract."

I made inline changes in the attached draft PDF (catalog-provenance-assertions-20261122.pdf). If GlobalBank requires binary-level signatures for every pinned model, we should treat that as a security add-on and scope a one-time attestation fee.

If this sounds good I can convert into final wording and Sean can send back to the customer.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Counsel, Data & Product | Redwood Inference
(attachment: catalog-provenance-assertions-20261122.pdf)

Subject: Re: Model catalog provenance + version pinning questionnaire

Lisa — thanks for your patience. Attached is our completed workbook (GlobalBank_RFI_model_catalog_answers_v1.xlsx) and a short provenance assertions brief (catalog-provenance-assertions-20261122.pdf) with the legal-approved language Monica suggested. Summary of key deliverables provided:

- Catalog metadata: every model entry in the Redwood catalog includes origin URL, model digest (SHA256), license identifier and license text, curator notes, and a link to the provenance certificate when available.
- SBOMs: we provide a serving-stack SBOM (package names + versions) for each catalog item by default. Training-data provenance is surfaced via curator-supplied tags; raw datasets are not provided.
- Pinning & signed manifests: customers may pin model versions via Console or API. For pinned versions we can provide a signed manifest (PKCS7) that includes model digest, build timestamp, serving binary id, and signing authority. HSM-backed signing is available as an enterprise add-on.
- Retention & audit evidence: signed manifests and provenance certificates are retained for two years by default; longer retention can be negotiated. We deliver evidence as time-stamped Drive links and, on request, notarized PDFs.

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm whether your auditor requires HSM-backed binary signatures per pinned model or if a signed manifest + Drive link is sufficient.
- If you want formal attestations (HSM signing), we can provide a pricing estimate and timeline via procurement.

Links and attachments:
- Completed workbook: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/GlobalBank/RFI-20261122/GlobalBank_RFI_model_catalog_answers_v1.xlsx
- Provenance brief (signed): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/GlobalBank/RFI-20261122/catalog-provenance-assertions-20261122.pdf

Happy to hop on a quick call next week with Monica & Neha if your auditor wants to walk through evidence formats.

Thanks,
Sean
